raw_case_text:
A 28-year-old male patient with a previous history of immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP), diagnosed six years ago but had stopped had treatment approximately five years ago, was hospitalized with clinical and epidemiological diagnosis of arbovirus infection (fever, asthenia, myalgia and arthralgia). On admission, thrombocytopenia (12,000/mm3) and anemia (8.0 g/dL) were observed (Table 1). Oral corticosteroid therapy was started with prednisone 1 mg/kg/day. On the third day of hospitalization, he had headache with vomiting, associated with mental confusion and, subsequently, motor aphasia and right hemiplegia. Considering the sudden worsening of the patient's overall conditions, he was referred to the intensive care unit. Nuclear magnetic resonance imaging of the brain was performed to rule out acute ischemic or hemorrhagic events. The neuroimaging examination showed no alterations. Faced with an acute neurological worsening, the possibility of TTP was considered. Analysis of the peripheral smear showed innumerable schizocytes, confirming the presence of TMA. Plasmapheresis and pulse therapy with methylprednisolone were started due to the hypothesis of TTP.
Serological results were IgM positive for chikungunya and dengue viruses, and initially, the presence of IgG only raised to chikungunya virus (Euroimmun Medizinische Labordiagnostika, Lubeck, Germany). Serological tests for hepatitis virus B and C were negative, as well as for retroviruses (only HIV). Regarding retroviruses, other representatives are not routinely investigated and, in this case, they were not suspected. The patient also had negative results for antinuclear antibody (ANA) (Table 2). During the follow-up, serological results for dengue and chikungunya were confirmed, at this time showing the presence of IgG antibodies to chikungunya as well as to dengue virus. The serological test for zika virus was not performed following guidelines from Brazilian Ministry of Health, which recommend not to test zika virus when serological tests for dengue and chikungunya are positive.
There was a decrease in lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) (Table 1). Plasmapheresis was maintained until platelet counts remained higher than 150,000 for three consecutive days (Figure 1). Complete remission of neurological signs occurred after the first plasmapheresis.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 28-year-old male presented with acute fever, asthenia, myalgia, and arthralgia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient was hospitalized with acute fever, asthenia, myalgia, and arthralgia suggestive of arboviral infection and found to have severe thrombocytopenia and anemia, for which oral prednisone (1 mg/kg/day) was started. On hospital day 3, he acutely deteriorated with headache, vomiting, mental confusion, motor aphasia, and right hemiplegia, requiring transfer to the intensive care unit.
subjective.past_medical_history: Immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) diagnosed 6 years prior; off treatment for approximately 5 years.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, asthenia, myalgia, arthralgia, and subsequent headache, vomiting, confusion, motor aphasia, and right-sided weakness.

objective.physical_examination: On hospital day 3: mental confusion, motor aphasia, and right hemiplegia.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission blood counts: severe thrombocytopenia (12,000/mm3) and anemia (hemoglobin 8.0 g/dL), with elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH). Peripheral blood smear (day 3): innumerable schistocytes confirming thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA). Viral serologies (hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and HIV): negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain MRI (day 3): normal, ruling out acute ischemic stroke or intracranial hemorrhage. Autoimmune testing: antinuclear antibody (ANA) negative.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) / thrombotic microangiopathy secondary to acute chikungunya and dengue virus co-infection. Acute ischemic/hemorrhagic stroke, HIV, hepatitis B and C, and SLE were ruled out. Confirmation: Peripheral blood smear showing numerous schistocytes with anemia, severe thrombocytopenia, elevated LDH, and acute neurological deficits, alongside positive IgM serology for both chikungunya and dengue viruses and subsequent IgG seroconversion for both viruses (Euroimmun ELISA). Management and outcome: Initiated on oral prednisone (1 mg/kg/day) at admission, then escalated on day 3 to therapeutic plasmapheresis and intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy. Complete remission of neurological deficits occurred after the first plasmapheresis session; daily plasmapheresis was continued until platelet counts remained >150,000/mm3 for 3 consecutive days with normalization of LDH.
